infra_note: Second working KL/steering-family run after NPO. Required two more fixes beyond the NPO infra: (1) module_regex needed an optional (base_model\.model\.)? prefix to match PEFT-wrapped module names (re.fullmatch was failing against 'base_model.model.model.layers.7'); (2) trainable_params_regex changed from '.*' to '.*lora.*', since RMU's create_optimizer explicitly re-enables requires_grad on every regex-matched param, and '.*' would have silently re-enabled gradients on the entire frozen base model, undoing LoRA's memory savings; (3) ref_act needed explicit dtype cast to model_act.dtype in rmu.py's retain-loss loop -- the 8-bit reference model's dequantized activations are fp16 internally regardless of the trainable model's bf16 dtype, causing 'Found dtype Half but expected BFloat16' during backward when mixed in a differentiable op.
interpretation: RGU (targeted scenario) numbers are EXACTLY unchanged from baseline -- at this gentle dose (steering_coeff=2, layer 7 only, 8 steps, LoRA r=16), RMU's activation-steering objective produced no measurable effect, gentler than both GA and NPO at their matched doses. Consistent with the RMU/WMDP literature's typical use of higher steering coefficients and/or more steps than tested here. train_loss ended at 0.0021 (small by design -- RMU's loss is an L2-style activation-matching objective, not cross-entropy, so magnitude isn't directly comparable to GA/NPO's loss values). This gives a genuine three-way comparison point for the diagnostic table: GA ranges from collapse (aggressive) to no-effect (gentle), NPO shows small non-degenerate movement at a matched gentle dose, RMU shows no movement at a matched gentle dose -- a real, reportable spectrum of method sensitivity, not yet a full hyperparameter-matched comparison (each method's 'gentle' dose was reached by different tuning, not a shared step/coefficient budget).
